subject: health
unitTitle: Substance Use, Community Risk, and Harm-Reduction Literacy
title: Guided practice: harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them
focus: harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them
essentialQuestion: What does the evidence say actually reduces harm, and what only sounds tough?
privacySafeScenario: Evaluate two fictional community prevention campaigns against stated evidence criteria, then redesign the weaker one and state how its effect would be measured.
studentTask: Learner applies harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them to a new fictional scenario and records the response with the reasoning, evidence, or decision process behind it.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them, then name one check that would catch a weak claim or an unsafe step.
completionCriteria: The learner completes the central task about harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them without being asked for any private disclosure.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a documented process, or a cited source rather than an unsupported claim.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
adaptationChoices: Evaluation and redesign may be written, storyboarded, dictated, or completed on a supplied criteria template.
extensionChallenge: Apply harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them under a new constraint, compare two approaches, or explain the idea to someone else with an original fictional example, without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
Evaluation and redesign may be written, storyboarded, dictated, or completed on a supplied criteria template.
trustedAdultNote: This course teaches health information and does not diagnose; direct urgent safety or health concerns to a trusted adult or qualified professional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice one safe, optional example of harm-reduction concepts and the arguments made for and against them in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or private disclosure is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
